newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austrian searchers locate Danube tug wreck - agency.
newsitem.headline: Austrian searchers locate Danube tug wreck - agency.

text.p: Austrian shipping authorities believe they have located the wreck of a Slovak tug that sank with eight crew on Tuesday after hitting a weir in the rain-swollen river Danube, domestic news agency APA said on Sunday.
Search teams had spotted oil on the river's surface which they suspect is coming from the the 130-tonne, Slovak-registered Dumbier, the agency quoted a search agency spokesman as saying.

He said the tug and the bodies of the eight crew were probably lying at least 100 metres (325 feet) under Vienna's unfinished Freudenau power plant near the weir.One crew reached safety on Tuesday and was recovering in a Vienna hospital.
Authorities said they would probably not be able to recover the wreck for at least a week because of the difficult conditions.
The accident blocked all commercial shipping traffic on Europe's busiest east-west waterway for days but officials said traffic would not be affected by the recovery efforts.

The 35-metre (115-ft) boat had been pushing a barge loaded with 750 tonnes of fishmeal. It sank after crashing into floodgates and then forcing its way through the wier, driven by the river's fierce current.
